blocks.title: Firewalls, IDS/IPS, and Web Filtering comparison
Firewalls, IDS/IPS, and Web Filtering exam shortcuts
items: Need to allow one service and block another → FIREWALL RULE
Modify traffic policy by port, protocol, source, or destination.
Example: Permit TCP 443 and block TCP 23.
Public web server should not sit on internal LAN → SCREENED SUBNET
Place public-facing systems in a DMZ-like perimeter zone.
Example: Internet users reach the web server without direct access to internal systems.
Known exploit needs immediate detection/blocking → SIGNATURE
Update or enable the IDS/IPS signature that matches the attack.
Example: IPS blocks traffic matching a known exploit signature.
Many users need one centralized web-control point → PROXY
A centralized proxy can inspect and filter web traffic.
Example: Corporate users browse through one secure web gateway.
Known phishing link must be blocked → URL SCANNING / BLOCK RULE
Inspect the URL and deny known malicious destinations.
Example: A phishing domain is added to a block list.
Unknown site has poor trust score → REPUTATION
Use reputation data to help decide whether access should be denied.
Example: A newly registered malicious domain receives a low reputation score.
blocks.example: Focus on what needs to be changed: traffic rules, detection logic, protocol choice, filtering policy, endpoint response, or user-behavior controls.

questions.q: A firewall should permit HTTPS traffic but block Telnet. Which capability should be modified?
questions.explanation: Firewall rules control traffic based on ports, protocols, sources, and destinations.

questions.q: A public web server should be reachable from the internet without exposing the internal LAN directly. Where should it be placed?
questions.explanation: A screened subnet or DMZ separates public-facing systems from internal networks.

questions.q: An IPS needs to block a newly recognized exploit pattern. What should be updated or enabled?
A company wants one central system to inspect employees' web requests. Which control fits best?
questions.explanation: A centralized proxy provides one central inspection and filtering point.

questions.q: A phishing domain should be denied whenever users try to browse to it. Which web-filtering capability is most direct?
questions.explanation: URL scanning and block rules can identify and deny known malicious destinations.

questions.q: A website is newly registered and has a very poor trust score. Which control can use that information?
questions.explanation: Reputation systems score domains or URLs based on trust or risk.
